note: Where to find Spanish to listen to and read. Edit this file to change the list; no code changes needed. The rule for picking: you should mostly understand it, and you should actually want to.

levels.name: Made for learners
levels.blurb: The gentlest start. They slow down and use pictures.

levels.name: Made for children
levels.blurb: Simple grammar, repeated constantly, short enough to finish.

levels.name: Made for everyone else
levels.blurb: For when you can follow the gist.

sources.name: Dreaming Spanish
sources.note: Graded from complete beginner to advanced. The most recommended thing there is

sources.name: Easy Spanish
sources.note: Real street interviews, with subtitles in both languages

sources.name: Coffee Break Spanish
sources.note: Short and structured, half English at first

sources.name: Duolingo Spanish Podcast
sources.note: True stories told in easy Spanish, with English narration

sources.name: Language Transfer
sources.note: A free audio course built on reasoning, not memorizing

sources.name: Pocoyó
sources.note: Almost no dialogue. Great at the very start

sources.name: Short Stories in Spanish (Olly Richards)
sources.note: Graded readers built for exactly this

sources.name: Something you already know, dubbed
sources.note: A show or film you've seen in English. Knowing the plot does the work subtitles would

sources.name: Radio Ambulante
sources.note: Real journalism and proper stories, worth hearing for their own sake

sources.name: Shows and films from Spain, Mexico and Argentina
sources.note: The accents differ, and that's worth hearing early

sources.name: Music you actually like
sources.note: Music is mostly for fun & new vocab and slang. Not recommended as a main source of native input
